maintenance.title: maintenance
maintenance.intro: During a maintenance window checks keep running but the covered monitors show as maintenance: no incidents are opened and no alerts are sent, and those checks don't count toward uptime. If a monitor is still down when the window ends, the alert fires then.
maintenance.dialogText: Alerts are paused for the selected monitors while the window is active.
maintenance.name: name
maintenance.monthDaysHint: Months without that day are skipped.
maintenance.labelsHint: Groups and tags also cover monitors added to them later.

groups.title: groups & tags
groups.intro: A monitor belongs to at most one group and can have any number of tags. Groups are sections on the dashboard and on status pages; both can be used to pick monitors for maintenance windows and to filter the monitor list.
groups.noTags: no tags yet. you can also create them from the monitor form.
groups.deleteGroupText: Its monitors are kept, without a group. The group is removed from maintenance windows and status pages.
groups.deleteTagText: The tag is removed from every monitor and maintenance window.
groups.groupDialogText: Pick the monitors in this group. A monitor moved here leaves its previous group.
groups.name: name
groups.tagDialogText: Tags are free labels, like the environment or the team.

agents.title: agents
agents.intro: Agents are tiny probes you run anywhere (VPS, home lab, another cloud region) to check your monitors from more than one place. The hub itself is always available as the built-in location.
agents.devBuild: development build: agents are not updated
agents.updateHint: agents installed with the script update to this version when they connect. Docker agents update with the image.
agents.empty: no agents yet. add one to monitor from a second location.
agents.rotateText: The current token stops working immediately and the agent disconnects. You will get new install commands.
agents.deleteText: The agent is disconnected and removed from all monitors. Past results are kept.
agents.dialogText: The location label is what you see on charts, e.g. "Frankfurt".

agents.installText: Run one of these on the machine that should become a monitoring location.
agents.waiting: waiting for {name} to connect… you will be asked which monitors should use it.

agentInstall.hint: The agent only dials out to the hub over HTTPS/WebSocket: no ports to open. The token is shown only now; rotate it to get a new one.

notifications.title: notifications
notifications.intro: Pick for each channel which monitors it covers (all of them, also future ones, or some groups and tags) and which events it gets; a monitor can also be linked to a channel one by one. A channel can wait before alerting, to escalate long outages to another contact, and repeat the alert while the monitor stays down.
notifications.empty: no channels. you won't be alerted when something breaks.
notifications.dialogText: Use "send test" to check the configuration before saving.
notifications.name: name
notifications.delayHint: Minutes down before the first alert. 0 = right away. With a delay the channel only hears about outages still going on by then: use it for an escalation contact.
notifications.repeatHint: 0 = once. Otherwise a reminder is sent while the monitor stays down (at least {min}).
notifications.pushOff: Push notifications to the mobile app are off: turn them on in <settings>Settings, mobile app</settings> to enable this channel.

hints.resendKey: Create a key with sending access in <link>Resend, API keys</link>. The from address must be on a domain verified in Resend.

mobileApp.title: mobile app
mobileApp.intro: Send alerts to the pingtxt app on your team's phones. Notifications go through a push relay, which holds the app's Firebase key. The relay stores nothing: it has no database, it only forwards each message to Firebase and does not log its text (monitor names, errors) or the phones' tokens.
mobileApp.enabled: push notifications to the mobile app
mobileApp.relayHint: The official relay works with the app from the App Store.
mobileApp.relayChanged: A different relay registers this hub again: every phone has to enroll again (the app does it on its next start).

mobileApp.notRegistered: Not registered: turning push on registers this hub with the relay.
mobileApp.channelHint: Then add a "pingtxt app" channel in notifications to choose who gets the alerts.

backups.exportIntro: monitors, groups, tags, notification channels, maintenance windows, status pages, agents and instance settings as a JSON file. no history and no user accounts: use a database backup for that.
backups.withSecretsHint: the file will hold passwords, bot tokens, secret webhook urls, login client secrets and agent tokens. keep it safe.
backups.withoutSecretsHint: passwords, tokens and secret webhook urls are replaced by [redacted]. importing here keeps the stored values; on another hub those channels are skipped and those monitors paused until you fill them in.
backups.mergeHint: objects with the same name are updated, the others are added. nothing is deleted.
backups.replaceHint: deletes every monitor (with its history), group, tag, channel, maintenance window and status page first.
backups.applySettings: also apply instance settings (public url, login, retention...)
backups.noAutoBackup: no automatic backup with this database: back up the database server first if you may want to undo the import.
backups.autoBackup: a database backup is taken before importing.
backups.replaceText: Every current monitor, with its history, and every group, tag, channel, maintenance window and status page will be deleted, then the file is imported.
backups.restartToRestore: restart the hub to finish the restore
backups.dbIntro: a backup is a full copy of the database: settings, users, secrets and history. it is taken while the hub keeps running.
backups.pending: restore pending: <hl>{name}</hl> replaces the database when the hub restarts. the current database is kept as a pre-restore backup.
backups.restoreText: The database will be replaced by {name} when the hub restarts. Everything after {date} is lost; the current database is kept as a pre-restore backup.
backups.serverIntro: this hub stores its data in {db}. back up the database server with its own tools (or your provider's snapshots): the dump holds settings, users, secrets and history. the configuration export above works too, without history and users. with the docker compose files from the docs:

kumaImport.intro: Upload a backup file from Uptime Kuma 1.x (Settings → Backup → Export). You see what will be created before anything changes. Groups and tags come along, paused monitors stay paused; notification channels are not imported.
